subject: Acme Health  Post-call: model fit, streaming UX notes & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@acmehealth.com>, Samuel Diaz <sam.diaz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health  Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Olivia / Sam 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared action plan.

Recap
- Goal: Evaluate streaming transcript generation for triage workflows (short clinical summaries, partial streaming to UI).
- Main concerns you raised: 1) partial output coherence during streaming (sentences cut mid-thought), 2) stop sequences not reliably ending generation on structured fields, 3) tail latency on longer sessions.
- Data: you shared a sample transcript during the call  helpful to reproduce behavior.

Proposed next steps (mutual)
1) We'll run a short model-fit evaluation across 3 candidate models on a 100-case prompt set (we'll provide the prompts).
2) Focused streaming quality checks: streaming chunking, stop sequence reliability, and partial-output coherence metrics.
3) Baseline performance: collect token-latency distribution and end-to-end UI latency for 50 streamed sessions.
4) Recommend config changes and a canary plan for any rollout.

Attached: acme_health_prompt_set_v2.json (prompt variants we discussed). I'll follow up with recommended model variants and a short benchmark report by EOD tomorrow.

If this looks right, I'll schedule the short eval run and share the Drive folder with the results.

Thanks 
Marissa

From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health  Post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa  this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications:

- We definitely want the streaming UX to feel "live"  partial lines are fine but they should not cut mid-sentence or repeat fragments.
- Stop sequences matter for us because downstream parsers pick up the final structured fields (diagnosis code, urgency). If the model sometimes misses the stop token we end up with parsing errors.
- Latency: our target is 200-300ms median token latency for short bursts and p95 under 1s during sustained sessions.

I've attached a short sample transcript (acme_health_sample_transcript.txt) that reproduces the partial-word issue  you should be able to run it through your streaming harness.

Also: curious what models you plan to test. We're budget-sensitive, so if a 13B model barely outperforms a 7B quantized variant we'd prefer the cheaper option.

Olivia Turner
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health
olivia.turner@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment: acme_health_sample_transcript.txt (30KB sample)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@acmehealth.com>, Samuel Diaz <sam.diaz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health  Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Olivia  thanks for the detail. Below are the candidate models and the quick plan. I'll run the evals today and upload a quick benchmark CSV to the shared Drive.

Candidate models to test
- redwood/rw-4o-13b: high-quality streaming variant (baseline for quality).
- redwood/servo-7b-quant: 7B quantized variant optimized for low cost and improved token throughput.
- open/gpt-3.5-std (hosted): lower-cost baseline for comparison (no private data footprint).

What we'll measure
- Streaming coherence: sentence-completion ratio (percent of sentences that are completed without mid-sentence truncation).
- Stop-sequence reliability: percent of outputs that contain the exact stop token within the expected window.
- Latency: median/p95 token latency and end-to-end response completion latency.
- Regression check: compare against the baseline runs we keep in the Drive (acme_benchmark_results.csv) to flag any quality regression.

Initial findings (preview)
- On your sample transcript the 13B model gives the best coherence but the 7B-quant variant performs nearly as well for structured fields (stop tokens) while reducing cost ~40%.
- Partial-output repetition seems correlated with larger chunk sizes in the streaming config (we'll test smaller chunk sizes and prefix caching adjustments).

Proposed next actions (for this week)
1) We'll run 100-case batch across the three models and put results in the Drive folder (I'll post the CSV link).
2) Engineering check: Jordan/Vivek to test streaming chunking (default 256-token chunks -> try 64 and 128) and stop-sequence enforcement tweaks in the runtime.
3) If results look good, propose a small canary (5% traffic) with the 7B-quant variant + tuned streaming config.

Deliverables & timing
- Benchmark CSV + short executive summary: EOD Tue (10 Mar).
- Recommended canary config: follow-up email + rollout plan by Wed 11 Mar.

Let me know if you want any additional metrics included.

Thanks 
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
